description_full: Open Text Corporation provides data management solutions for enterprise AI in North, Central and South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Australia, Japan, Singapore, India, and China. Its products and solutions help organizations collect, connect, contextualize, protect, govern, use, and secure data across their operations. The company offers cloud services and subscriptions, including software as a service offerings, application programming interfaces and data services, and private cloud products, such as hosted services and managed service arrangements; foundational platform of technology services; and packaged business applications, as well as managed services and outsourced B2B integration solutions, including program implementation, operational management, and customer support. It also engages in licensing software products to customers; and consulting and learning services, such as implementation, training, and integration of licensed product offerings into the customer's systems. In addition, the company offers content, business network, observability and service management, cybersecurity, application delivery management, and analytics. It has partnerships with SAP SE, Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Corporation, Oracle Corporation, and SALESFORCE, INC., as well as global systems integrators, including Accenture plc, Capgemini Technology Services SAS, Deloitte Consulting LLP, Hewlett Packard Enterprises, and Tata Consultancy Services. The company serves global 10,000 organizations, enterprise companies, public sector agencies, mid-market companies, SMBS, and direct consumers. The company has a strategic partnership with Cohere to develops and provides agentic AI to governments and regulated industries. Open Text Corporation was incorporated in 1991 and is headquartered in Waterloo, Canada.

financial_summary: Open Text Corporation is a mid-cap technology business with a $6.0B market cap on $5.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 68% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $808M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.4× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 3.4×.
Management returns a meaningful 10.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.0% of the shares.

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 24% over the past year excluding the latest month.

val: The stock trades 75% below its DCF fair value of $98.52, a meaningful margin of safety.

On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 9.4 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 6.8 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 7.4 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 62% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 13.4% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 10.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 11 covering analysts target $28.14 on average, 13% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 8% falls short of the cost of capital of 8.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.50).
It runs a 68% gross margin and converts 15% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 9/9 and cash conversion of 1.57x.
ROE of 16% is amplified by 3.3x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
It spends 12.3% of revenue on R&D and 1.5% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.4x net debt to EBITDA ($956.0M of cash against $5.8B of debt), with interest covered 3.4x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.24 in the distress zone.
The current ratio of 0.81 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 56% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.4% over 3 years, 9.2% over 5 years and 11.1% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Free cash flow has compounded -0.1% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.03, a backlog worth 47% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 2%.
Capex runs only 0.1x depreciation (3.8% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 23, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 12.5% on average.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.0%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
It returns 10.5% a year to shareholders (6.0% in buybacks and 4.5% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 2.3% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years, raising it 5.0% a year over the last five.
people: With about 19,500 employees, each generates about $269K of revenue, 0.7x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 11.8% a year across its filed history.
